title: Upstream compiler progress is rolled back as downstream unittest regression

dynamic_evidence.downstream_effect: unittest still failed because remaining moon_phase.cpp compile blocker prevented the shared CMake build

root_cause.mechanism: _workspace_quality_repair_effect evaluates workspace_quality_verifier_regressed before checking an explicit reduction in upstream compiler barrier identities. Derivative unittest setup errors therefore override real compiler progress and force candidate rollback.
root_cause.why_general: Any project whose test runner invokes a shared build can report more downstream test errors while an edited source file has already left the compiler failure frontier. Counting downstream fanout before compiler-frontier reduction loses valid same-task repair progress across languages and build systems.

hypothesis: If the same authoritative compile verifier reports a strict subset of explicit failing translation-unit identities after a real write, classify the candidate as accepted progress before derivative unittest fanout; true test-only regressions must remain regression.

planned_fix.behavior: Preserve candidates only when an explicit FAILING_TUS set strictly decreases for the same verifier command. Return progress, not forward_unmask, because residual compile identities are already-seen diagnostics and the oscillation gate intentionally rejects non-novel forward-unmask phases. Do not reorder generic diagnostic progress ahead of regression and do not relax unittest discovery/fanout guards without compiler-frontier evidence.

required_verification: TDD RED proves current effect is regression for 3-to-2 FAILING_TUS plus derivative unittest fanout
GREEN proves effect is accepted progress
existing unittest fanout and discovery-collapse regression tests remain green
ruff, format, mypy and targeted pytest evidence
